items.title: How FedEx’s CSO engineers sustainability into long-term strategy
items.summary: FedEx has significantly expanded its purchases of unblended sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) with contracts to buy more than 20 million gallons for use at five major U.S. airports in California, Florida, New Jersey, New York and Texas through 2027.

items.title: What’s next for the 100% renewable energy movement
items.summary: Ten years ago, HP Inc. pledged to match 100 percent of its global electricity with renewables by 2025, as part of an early wave of corporate commitments inspired by the Climate Group’s RE100 campaign.

items.title: Government backs £90m heat network expansion to cut energy bills
items.summary: The UK Government has announced a £90m investment to support new and upgraded heat networks, helping to bring bills down for over 750,000 homes.

items.title: Nature-related disclosures double year on year, TNFD report finds
items.summary: Yet, disclosure quality remains uneven. As companies grapple with reporting frameworks, a significant appetite for mandatory standards is emerging.

items.title: From simplification to segmentation: Why ESRS-40a matters for UK businesses
items.summary: Over the past year, many organisations have welcomed headlines suggesting sustainability reporting is becoming simpler.

items.title: NEXT WEEK: What does a revised ISO 14001 mean for sustainability professionals?
items.summary: On 29 September, edie is hosting a webinar in partnership with BSI to explore changes to the ISO 14001 standard addressing environmental management.

items.title: Road to COP31: World must double renewable build-out to hit 2030 goal
items.summary: Despite record-high deployment, a new report from the COP31 Presidency, the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) and the Global Renewables Alliance (GRA) has concluded that annual build-out must virtually double to meet 2030 targets.

items.title: EU consults on minimum energy and water standards for data centres
items.summary: The European Commission is consulting on proposals to introduce a rating scheme for data centres similar to how buildings have minimum performance standards on energy efficiency.

items.title: How can supply chains be designed for resilience in an increasingly disrupted world?
items.summary: Resilience is becoming a design challenge for supply chains as climate disruption, geopolitical instability, energy volatility and resource constraints compete for attention at board level, according to Maxfield Weiss, global head of sustainability at the Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply (CIPS).

items.title: Explainer: How sea level rise poses an ‘existential threat’ to humans, heritage and nature
items.summary: For millions of people around the world, rising sea levels are already reshaping economies, livelihoods and cultures.
